rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Possessive attribution to God does not make a term such as 'shin' a divine part; each relation is determined by its terms, since God is indivisible.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ tecezzîden münezzeh ehaddir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'Rolling up the shin' can mean preparing, gathering oneself, taking care, or approaching a task with urgency and intensity.
rows.anchor: “Teşmîr-i sâk”, paçayı sıvamak veya çemremek, yerine göre toplanmak, hazırlanmak, mahzurdan sakınarak cidd ü ihtimam ile işe sıvanmak, şiddet ibraz etmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'Uncovering the shin' depicts a hidden reality beginning to reveal itself clearly, from within outward or from below upward, with forceful emotional impact.
rows.anchor: “keşf-i sâk” veya “keşf an sâk” mestur bir hakikatin, içerden dışarıya, aşağıdan yukarıya doğru bir uçtan kendini vuzuh ile basar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Expressions of the shin becoming visible can share the sense of clarity yet differ in emotional effect; the effect depends on the reality revealed and the observer's relation to it.
rows.anchor: “Harb sâkını keşfetti”, “falan kahraman baldırını açıverdi” denilmekle “zafer sâkını açtı, murad bir uçtan kendini gösterdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an's image of Bilqis exposing her shins in 27:44 signifies her weakness and vulnerability, not her strength.
rows.anchor: Belkıs’ın baldırlarını açması onun kuvvetini değil, zaafını kusurunu anlatmıştı

rows.speaker: Keşşâf
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf's brief discussion points to both aspects of the expression: its figurative usage and its intensity.
rows.anchor: Keşşâf’ın kısaca geçen beyânâtında bu iki cihete de işaret vardır.

rows.speaker: Rebî‘ b. Enes
rows.claim: Rebi b. Anas glosses the day as the time when the covering is uncovered and the veil lifted; Elmalılı reports this through Abd b. Humayd as cited by Alusi.
rows.anchor: Rebî‘b. Enes demiştir ki: “O gün gıtâ keşfolunacağı, perdenin açılacağı gündür.

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported by Bayhaqi to explain the phrase as the disclosure of the matter and the appearance of deeds.
rows.anchor: Beyhakī de İbn Abbas’tan حِيْنَ يُكْشَفُ الأَْمْرُ وَتـَبْدُو الأَْعْمَال emr keşf olunup

rows.speaker: Sa‘îd b. Cübeyr
rows.claim: Sa'id b. Jubayr rejects attributing a literal shin to God and says that only a severe matter is uncovered; Elmalılı says the hadith should be understood likewise.
rows.anchor: Sa‘îd b. Cübeyr, bu âyette “sâk”ın Allah teâlâ’ya izâfetini inkâr etmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı understands the uncovering as God's reality or judgment beginning to appear from the unseen into the visible world, awaited by believers and dreaded by criminals.
rows.anchor: biz burada يَوْمَ يُكْشَفُ عَن سَاقٍۢ kavl-i celîlinde “keşf-i sâk”tan müslimin imanıyla beklediği, mücrimin kaçındığı Hakk’ın veya hükm-i Hakk’ın perde-i gaybdan sâha-i şuhûda kendini bir uçtan göstermeye başlaması

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The terrifying force of the disclosure is painful humiliation and crushing dread for criminals, but an enticing joy and honor for Muslims.
rows.anchor: mücrimlere mahz-ı elem olan hevl-engiz bir kahr u tezlil, müslimlere de aynı hâile içinde murad kapısını açan câzibeli bir şevk ve izzet heyecânı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is a severe warning to the criminals and their partners, while its address to the Prophet frames it as promise and glad tidings for believers.
rows.anchor: bu âyet müslimlere bir va‘d ü tebşir olmak üzere Peygamber’e hitab siyâkında vârid olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says فَلْيَأْتُوا is attached to يَوْمَ, though it may instead attach to an omitted اُذْكُرْ or to the later تَرْهَقُهُمْ.
rows.anchor: اُذْكُرْ gibi bir mahzûfa da yahut gelecek تَرْهَقُهُمْ fiiline de ta‘alluk edebilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the resurrection the deniers are summoned, individually or in groups, to submit and prostrate as a rebuke, but cannot raise their heads or bend their backs.
rows.anchor: ne başlarını kaldırabilecekler, ne bellerini eğebilecekler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their eyes are humbled and they are so abased that they cannot even gesture; humiliation keeps engulfing them.
rows.anchor: kendilerini bir zillet saracak da saracak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In worldly life they were safely and freely invited to prostrate and obey, but rejected the invitation and failed to value its reward or their safety.
rows.anchor: Hâlbuki vaktiyle dünyada başları selâmette iken o secdeye davet olunuyorlardı tav‘an secde ve inkıyad etmeleri kendilerine teklif olunuyordu da onu reddediyorlardı.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They thought sinners were wiser than believers; now they will long to perform the very prostration they once refused, but will be powerless and defeated.
rows.anchor: O selâmetin kadrini bilmiyorlar, rızâ ve ihtiyarlarıyla secdeye yanaşmıyorlar, itaatin sevâbına âkıbette zevkine inanmıyorlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tells Muhammad to leave the deniers of the Qur'an to Him; they call it old tales, reject obedience and afterlife judgment, and he should continue his mission without distress or fear.
rows.anchor: O hâlde benimle bırak bu hadîsi tekzib edeni bu Kur’ân’a inanmayan, “eskilerin masalları” diyen, secde ve itaatin lüzûmuna kāil olmayan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gradually draws the deniers toward punishment without their awareness by increasing the wealth, power, and pleasures they mistake for good fortune.
rows.anchor: Biz onları bilemeyecekleri cihetten istidrac ederiz haklarında iyi zannettikleri aldatıcı bazı servetler, kuvvetler, zevkler vererek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives them a longer leash and reprieves them; they take the delay as gain and indulge, thinking they have escaped.
rows.anchor: Ve Ben onların iplerini uzatırım, istediklerine bırakıvermişim gibi imhâl ederim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's stratagem is firm because His knowledge encompasses every state and His plan is secure; at the appointed time He suddenly pulls them down to their end.
rows.anchor: çünkü fendim sağlamdır. İlmim muhît, tedbîrim muhkemdir. Her lahzada her hâllerini bilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad asks no fee for his counsel and guidance, so the opponents are not burdened by a debt to him; his reward belongs to God.
rows.anchor: Yoksa onlardan bir ecir mi istiyorsun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their losses and hostility arise from their own foolishness, immoral living, wastefulness, and being deceived by partners, not from the Prophet's message.
rows.anchor: onların borçlanmaları ve çektikleri garâmet ve belâ kendi akılsızlıkları, ahlâksızlıkları, sefâhetleri sebebiyle ve uydukları şerîklere aldanmaları yüzündendir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers do not possess God's unseen knowledge or the Supreme Pen recording the Preserved Tablet, and cannot decree that their crimes are good or escape judgment.
rows.anchor: Allah’a mahsus olan gayb ilmi onların yanında, Levh-i Mahfûz’u yazan Kalem-i A‘lâ onların elinde de artık kâinâtın mukadderâtını

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paired questions gather the argument back to the sura's opening oath by the pen, which Elmalılı identifies as the Supreme Pen recording the unseen decrees of the universe.
rows.anchor: sûrenin başındaki وَٱلْقَلَمِ وَمَا يَسْطُرُونَ âyetine kadar ircâ‘etmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad should bear God's judgment patiently, including the delay in destroying deniers and the hardships of prophethood, and await its eventual execution.
rows.anchor: Rabbinin hükmüne sabret onları hemen mahvedivermeyip imhâl buyurmasına ve seni tükenmez ecre nâil etmek için

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The 'companion of the fish' is Jonah, whom 37:142 describes as swallowed by the fish while blameworthy.
rows.anchor: “Sâhib-i Hût” Sûre-i Saffât’ta فَٱلْتَقَمَهُ ٱلْحُوتُ وَهُوَ مُلِيمٌۭ [37/142] buyurulduğu üzere Yûnus aleyhisselâm’dır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Hut is the famous fish that held Jonah in its belly and is also called al-Nun.
rows.anchor: “el-Hût” onun karnında habsolunduğu meşhur olan balıktır ki ona “en-Nûn” da denilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say dhu is stronger than sahib in meaning; calling Jonah Dhu al-Nun suggests his release from the fish, while Sahib al-Hut emphasizes his being held inside it.
rows.anchor: “Zû” dahi mâlum ki sâhip mânasınadır. Demişlerdir ki “zû” “sâhib”den eblağdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah is called Dhu al-Nun in praise in 21:87, but Sahib al-Hut here as the example Muhammad must avoid, signaling his state of captivity.
rows.anchor: Onun için Sûre-i Enbiyâ’da medholunurken “Zü’n-nûn”, burada ona benzemekten nehyolunurken “Sâhib-i Hût” tesmiye edilmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because both hut and nun mean fish, mentioning Sahib al-Hut indirectly alludes to the sura's opening nun.
rows.anchor: Bunda “hût” ve “nûn” ikisi de balık mânasına olmak itibariyle

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: Some interpreters identify the opening nun as the fish in which Jonah was confined.
rows.anchor: Bundan bazıları نٓ’dan murad bu hût olduğuna zâhib olmuşlardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı rejects the fish as the primary meaning of nun because, on that reading, the verse would more fittingly say Sahib al-Nun, though an allusion remains.
rows.anchor: Lâkin öyle olsa idi burada “sâhibi’n-nûn” denilmek muvâfık olurdu.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad must patiently bear God's decree rather than repeat Jonah's impatience and angry withdrawal from his people; the command nevertheless points to Jonah at the moment he called upon God.
rows.anchor: Sabırsızlıkla kavmine kızıp öfke ile zulümâtta habse düşen Yûnus gibi olma, hiçbir vechile onun gibi olma değil, ancak şu hâl ve vakitteki Yûnus gibi olma

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Makzum describes Jonah calling out with his breath choked by anger; the point is his state, not the addressee or full content of the prayer.
rows.anchor: O vakit ki o, mekzum, yani öfke ile nefesi tıkanmış bir hâlde nidâ etmişti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse emphasizes Jonah's anguished cry rather than explaining to whom or how he prayed; his prayer was the confession that none is God but God and that he had wronged himself.
rows.anchor: Ma‘amâfîh burada maksud kime ve nasıl nidâ ettiğini anlatmak değil, yalnız öfke ile boğulacak bir hâlde nidâ etmiş olduğunu anlatmaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Had God's favor not reached Jonah by inspiring repentance and glorification and answering his prayer, he would have been cast into the open in a blameworthy condition.
rows.anchor: Eğer Rabbinin nimeti ona yetişmiş olmasa idi tevbe ve nedâmetle tesbîhi ilham edip duasına icâbetle imdad etmese idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah would have left the fish eventually, but without God's favor he would have emerged condemned rather than in a praiseworthy state; his anger and impatience were not good.
rows.anchor: Gerçi ilelebed balığın karnında kalmayacak, her ne olsa atılacaktı; lâkin iyi, memduh bir şey olarak değil, mezmum, fena bir hâlde atılacaktı.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God chose Jonah rather than leaving him in his former state, purified him, protected him from blame, freed him from grief and anger, and restored him to revelation.
rows.anchor: Fakat Rabbi onu ictibâ buyurdu o tabiatta bırakmadı, ıstıfâ eyledi, inayetiyle derdi topladı, süzdü, mezmum olmaktan korudu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made Jonah righteous to completion as a messenger, sent him to a hundred thousand people for prophethood and intercession, and thereby benefited them and saved them from punishment.
rows.anchor: Yüzbinlere risalet ve şefaat için gönderdi, onları o sebeple azabdan kurtarıp istifade ettirdi de kendisini salâhta kemâle ermiş mürselînden kıldı.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The universe unfolds through God's decree, which links past, present, and future while giving people agency and producing outcomes suited to each state; every moment remains under His judgment.
rows.anchor: Kâinat bu suretle kalem-i Hakk’ın yazdığı ve yazacağı satırların müfâdıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah's anger led to confinement in the fish and nearly to a blameworthy end, but God's countervailing favor outweighed the harm, rescued him, and purified him to full righteousness.
rows.anchor: Yûnus’un bir öfkesi kendisini balığın karnında habse düşürdü, o öfke ile kalsa idi az daha mezmum bir âkıbete düşecekti.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: States such as anger and patience are partly connected to divine predestination and partly to human choice.
rows.anchor: Öfke veya sabır gibi hâllerin bir ucu takdîr-i ilâhîde, bir ucu da insanın iradesine bağlanmıştır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad, purified and chosen with a greater bounty, must continue his prophetic duty with steadfastness, wait patiently for God's next judgment, and see how truth will appear.
rows.anchor: Yûnus gibi sabırsızlık etme de Rabbinin bugünkü hükmüne sabret. Vazifene kemâl-i metanet ile devam edip yarınki hükmünü gözet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sarsar is a wind that roars with a harsh sound or a very cold storm; Elmalılı renders the destruction as a violent wind and raging storm.
rows.anchor: Rîh-i sarsar şiddetli sesle gürleyen veya çok soğuk fırtına.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Atiya means rebellious and forceful, repeatedly overturning its victims with no means to resist or escape.
rows.anchor: Azgın büker büker atar, redd ü mukavemete ve halâsa çare bulunmaz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Husum can be a verbal noun for ill omen or repeated treatment, and also the plural of hasim; hasm means cutting something off at its root or cauterizing repeatedly, so here it means a continuous root-cutting storm.
rows.anchor: “Hasm” bir şeyi kökünden kesmek ve bir marazı kökünden kesmek için ard ardına dağlamak, mütetâbi‘an keyyetmek mânalarına gelir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says the root-cutting sense is figurative here and glosses the phrase as continuous action to cut off the people at their roots, connecting it to 54:19.
rows.anchor: köklerini kesmek için müstemirren demek

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: Some interpret husuman as ill-fated or unlucky days, in line with 41:16; this conveys a storm so ill-omened that it left no good behind.
rows.anchor: bazıları da “husûmen” menhûsât, meş’ûmât demek olduğunu söylemişlerdir.

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: Some analyze husuman as a verbal noun in the causal function maf'ul li-ajlihi, meaning that the storm came in order to cut them off at the root.
rows.anchor: masdar olarak mef‘ûl-i leh, yani köklerini kesmek için demek olduğuna zâhib olmuşlardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Expressions such as 'husum storm' and 'days of husum,' alongside berd al-ajuz, are established in Turkish usage.
rows.anchor: “Berdü’lacûze”, “husûm fırtınası”, “husûm günleri”, “eyyâm-ı husûm” tâbirleri lisânımızda da şâyi‘dir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sara is the plural of sari, meaning struck down and fallen; here it means dead.
rows.anchor: “Sarî‘”in cem‘idir. “Sarî‘” çarpılıp yere yıkılmış, burada helâk olmuş demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those before Pharaoh means earlier generations extending back to Noah's people; this is a generalization after the particular, with Ad and Thamud included.
rows.anchor: Ve ondan evvelkiler ta kavm-i Nûh’a kadar kurûn-i ûlâ. Burada tahsisten sonra ta‘mîm vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier generations include Ad and Thamud as well.
rows.anchor: Zira Âd ve Semûd da evvelkilerdendir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mutafikat refers to the villages of Lot's people, meaning their inhabitants; it is a specification after the generalization.
rows.anchor: Lût kavminin karyeleri ki murad ahâlisi olan kavm-i Lût’tur. Bu da ta‘mîmden sonra tahsistir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression's reversal and undulation vividly evoke the Haaqqa and the scenes of rebellion that caused it.
rows.anchor: İfadenin bu suretle alt üst edilerek dalgalandırılması

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khatia means an error, sin, or crime in the sense opposite to correctness rather than intention; here it is the crime of denial already mentioned.
rows.anchor: “kasd” mukabili değil de “savâb” mukabili hata, hatî’e ve cinayet işlemek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabiya is an increasing, overwhelming grip whose force rises in proportion to the degree of their disobedience.
rows.anchor: Gittikçe artan, mütezâyid onların isyanlarının ziyadeliği nisbetinde şiddeti artan kāhir bir kabza.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water's transgression refers to the time of Noah's flood.
rows.anchor: O su tuğyan ettiği vakit Yani Nûh’un tûfânı zamanında

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God preserved the audience in the loins of their believing ancestors while destroying the deniers, carrying their descendants forward rather than cutting off their line.
rows.anchor: tekzib eden diğerlerinin kökünü keserken sizin kökünüzü kesmedik de iman eden atalarınızın sulbünde taşıyarak muhafaza ettik.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-jariya means the flowing vessel and, with the definite article, refers to Noah's ark; calling a ship a jariya is conventional usage, as the cited line about ninety girls in a ship illustrates.
rows.anchor: Ahd ile “el-câriye”, Hazret-i Nûh’un gemisidir. Mutlaka gemiye “câriye” ıtlâkı da müte‘âreftir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited poetic line says 'ninety girls in the belly of a ship,' using jariya for a vessel.
rows.anchor: تِسْعُونَ جَارِيَةً فِي بَطْنِ جَارِيَةٍ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular definite al-jariya also hints that the people addressed were then preserved in the current of their ancestors' loins along with the ark.
rows.anchor: burada yalnız “el-câriye” denilmesinde onunla beraber muhatabların o vakit orada atalarının sulbündeki bir cereyanda mahfuz bulunduklarına da bir îmâ vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God, not the ark, was the true carrier and protector; the ark was an apparent means displaying divine power, and faith was the spiritual reason for boarding.
rows.anchor: Ona yüklemenin sebeb-i mânevîsi de iman idi. Hakīkī fâil ise Biz idik.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the flood and ark a lasting reminder for survivors and descendants of His power, wisdom, punishment, mercy, faith's benefit, rebellion's harm, and future protection.
rows.anchor: bir tezkire; unutulmayıp anılacak, önünde ve sonunda Bizim kudretimizi, sun‘u hikmetimizi, kahrımızın şiddetini ve rahmetimizin vüs‘atini

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder serves as a monument, admonition, and lesson passed from those who witnessed the event to those who did not; it is not knowable by reason alone.
rows.anchor: bir öğüt, bir ibret muhtırası kılalım da görenler görmeyenlere, duyanlar duymayanlara ansın, haber versin.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attentive ears listen, retain, reflect, act on, and transmit the reminder for later generations to benefit; heedless ears that deny it incur punishment.
rows.anchor: dinleyip, hıfzedip düşünerek mûcebince amel etsin, zâyi‘etmeyip ilerisi için istifade eylesin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accounts through this point are lesser resurrections serving as reminders; from here the sura begins its detailed treatment of the Great Resurrection, with trumpet passages in 27:87 and 39:68 as parallels.
rows.anchor: كَذَّبَتْ’den buraya kadar olan beyânât öyle muhtıra kabîlinden olan küçük kıyametler demek olup bundan itibaren Kıyâmet-i Kübrâ olan Hâkka’nın tafsîline şürû‘olunuyor
